title: Respect The Process - Andrew Dumit, Watershed Technology Inc.
talk_summary: Watershed replaced free-form ReAct tool-calling with a coding agent for editing large supply-chain graphs, then had to constrain it after it wrote wrong-language code, edited artifacts without lineage, and falsely claimed success. Their fix is a typed SDK as the only mutation door plus a deterministic post-run executor that lints, detects conflicts, runs the code, validates artifacts, and emits a human-reviewable report.

takeaways.technique: Typed SDK as the only mutation door
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents may write arbitrary code, but all state-changing operations must go through a typed SDK with edit primitives, assertions, and derived-vs-editable field enforcement; the SDK is the sole entry point.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic post-run executor owned by the harness
takeaways.what_they_do: On agent completion, a harness-owned script lints the agent's code, detects conflicting edits, executes it, validates output artifacts, and sends failures back to the agent instead of accepting the agent's self-report.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the real guarantee comes from the final script that we orchestrate on agent completion

takeaways.technique: Structured review artifact instead of raw code review
takeaways.what_they_do: Deterministic execution emits a summary artifact (functions applied, edit counts, aggregate impact, per-graph node-level detail) so reviewers validate outcomes without reading the generated code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: create a well-structured review artifact that makes it easy to review what the agent did without having to actually ever go read the underlying code
takeaways.numbers: 749 edit actions across 50 graphs; 45.6% emissions reduction reported in the artifact

takeaways.technique: Task-level eval set with hill-climbing loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They track success on an internal eval set of (graphs + goal) tasks and iterate on prompts, few-shots, SDK ergonomics, and plan/execute decomposition, moving accuracy from 43% to 92%.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've been able to improve our outcomes from about 43% to 92% on our set of internal evals

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of many context-heavy tool calls to explore data, the coding agent writes loops and scripts to unpack and summarize nodes, cutting context consumption and improving consistency across many graphs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It could write loops over graphs and nodes. It could write scripts to unpack and summarize the node content

takeaways.technique: Plan-then-execute decomposition plus elicited expert judgment
takeaways.what_they_do: They split the overall problem into a plan/execute loop and encode domain expert judgment (and prompts to elicit it from users) so the agent handles under-specified tasks more consistently.
